title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Several Services for a Dormant Account in One Contact
content:
A single contact with the owner of a dormant Savings & Money Market Accounts product can take in more than one of the product's services. This page describes how the work of such a contact is shared between the owner and the agent, what the different kinds of action touch, and how their postings behave in time. Every service keeps its own rules, and nothing here adds to them.

## Who acts

The owner in such a contact is one whose identity has been verified. Moving the owner's own money out of the account at the owner's instruction, by telephone, into a checking account of their own is the customer's own act: the agent hands that transfer over and the customer themselves performs it, and doing so is not a confirmation of anything the agent does. The records the bank keeps about the account itself, meaning its status, its tier and the fees charged to it or given back, are brought up to date by the agent.

## What the different kinds of action touch

A transfer out and a fee returned are both entries on the account's ledger, so each of them moves the balance, one down and the other up. A change of status touches only the account's status and its latest-activity date and leaves the ledger alone, while a change of tier touches the tier and nothing else.

## Timing

Each of these actions takes effect at the moment it is carried out; none of them waits on an outside event or on the passage of time. A posting made during a contact held on a business day, a weekday other than a Federal Reserve holiday, bears the contact day as its date, while one made when the bank is closed bears the next business day.
